versions.source: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual 8th Edition / NCCN / UICC
versions.provenance: 8th edition staging, verified against AJCC 8th edition / NCCN guidelines; licensed verification standard. Requires R1 clinical verification before unchecked use.
versions.introduction: Hodgkin lymphoma uses the Lugano modification of Ann Arbor staging, mapped here onto T/N/M slots for the overlay engine. Stage depends on nodal regions relative to the diaphragm, contiguous extranodal (E) extension, bulky mediastinal disease (X: mass ratio over 0.33 of thoracic diameter, or any mass 10 cm or larger) and spleen (S) involvement; A/B records absence or presence of B symptoms. Most patients present with contiguous spread from cervical/supraclavicular nodes, and FDG-PET/CT is standard for staging and interim response (Deauville score).

t.label: Extent of disease cannot be assessed
Involvement of a single lymphatic region (Stage I pattern)
Two or more lymphatic regions on the same side of the diaphragm (Stage II pattern)
Lymphatic regions on both sides of the diaphragm (Stage III pattern)

n.label: Two or more involved regions on the same side of the diaphragm
Involved regions on both sides of the diaphragm, and/or splenic involvement (S)

m.label: Disseminated extranodal disease (marrow, liver, lung, bone)

stageGroups.basis: One region, no B symptoms; IIA adds E or more regions same side
Same side of diaphragm, no B symptoms; add X if bulky
Same side of diaphragm with B symptoms and/or bulky X
Both sides of diaphragm, no B symptoms
Both sides of diaphragm with B symptoms

versions.regionalNodes: Cervical/supraclavicular, axillary, mediastinal/hilar, para-aortic, mesenteric, iliac and inguinal-femoral regions plus Waldeyer ring and spleen (S). A single extranodal extension (E) does not upstage to IV; diffuse extranodal disease does.
versions.histologicGrade: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma is not graded G1-G3; subtype (nodular sclerosis, mixed cellularity, lymphocyte-rich, lymphocyte-depleted) and nodular lymphocyte-predominant HL are the histologic classifiers. ESR, haemoglobin and albumin feed prognostic scores, not grade.
versions.histopathologicTypes: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma: nodular sclerosis, mixed cellularity, lymphocyte-rich, lymphocyte-depleted; nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (a distinct entity).
prognosticFactors: Bulky disease (X; mediastinal mass ratio over 0.33)
B symptoms (fever over 38 C, drenching sweats, weight loss over 10 percent in 6 months)
ESR, haemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte count (Hasenclever/IPS factors in advanced disease)
Early vs advanced presentation (defines ABVD vs escalated BEACOPP pathways)
